entities.summary: Giovanni Garzoni (1419–1506) was an Italian humanist and physician from Bologna, where he was professor of medicine and teacher of rhetoric. Born into a family of modest means, Garzoni's early education was facilitated by his talent and dedication. He later attended the University of Bologna, where he studied medicine and philosophy. In 1450, Garzoni became a lecturer at the University of Bologna, teaching medicine and philosophy to aspiring scholars. His expertise in humanism and medicine earned him recognition from the University and the Papal Court, where he served as a physician and advisor. Garzoni's contributions to the field of humanism and medicine were significant, as he helped to establish the University of Bologna as a center of learning and intellectual inquiry. He also played a key role in the development of the Renaissance humanist movement, which sought to revive classical learning and promote individualism. Garzoni's legacy extends beyond his academic achievements, as he was also a patron of the arts and a collector of rare books and manuscripts. His love of learning and his commitment to the pursuit of knowledge left a lasting impact on the world of scholarship and intellectual inquiry.
